deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to the 1974 'topologie modérée' (tame topology) notes. X is a topological space. F is a family of subsets of X (the candidate 'tame' or constructible sets) satisfying axioms a)–e) from the preceding pages. Axiom e) is a local condition: X is covered by opens U in F with A ∩ U in F.

What the previous page did. Assuming the opens in F form a basis of X, it formed the subsheaf of the sheaf P_X (germs of subsets of X) generated by F. Its global sections are a closure F-bar of F. When X is quasi-compact, F-bar = F.

This page drops the basis assumption.

1. A sheaf G_F is defined. Its sections over an open U are the subsets A of U that are locally in F: for every x in U there are a neighbourhood V_x and some B_x in F with A ∩ V_x = B_x ∩ V_x. In modern terms G_F is the sheafification, inside the sheaf of subsets, of the constant presheaf F.

2. Set F-bar = Γ(X, G_F), and more generally F-bar_U = Γ(U, G_F). F-bar again satisfies a)–d), and perhaps e). It is unclear whether F-bar is generated by its closed members.

3. Without the basis hypothesis, F-bar = F can fail even for compact X. Example: F = {∅, X}. Here F-bar is the set of clopen subsets of X. When X is locally connected, these are the unions of connected components.

4. Main case: F = C_P, the family generated by the cells (strata) of a cellular decomposition P of X. Question: when is F-bar = F?
   - Any clopen subset of a closed cell lies in F-bar. Near points of the closed cell it agrees locally with the closed cell or with ∅; near points outside it is locally empty. So closed cells must be connected.
   - Suppose we want F-bar_U = F_U for every open U in F. Each cell is closed in some open U in F (e.g. a star-type neighbourhood). So every cell must itself be connected.
   - The page ends asking whether connectedness of all cells is sufficient.

5. The next page answers this. Reducing to U = X, a set A that is locally a union of strata (leaves) is globally one, because A ∩ X_i is clopen in the connected stratum X_i. For general U, elements of F-bar_U are unions of connected components of the X_i ∩ U. The converse fails (example: the strata {0} and R \ {0} in R).

Purpose. This is foundational bookkeeping for a sheaf-theoretic notion of 'locally tame / constructible subset' relative to a stratification. The key point is that stratification-constructibility is local exactly when the strata are connected.
errors: Small gap: 'toute partie ouverte et fermée d'une cellule fermée est dans F-bar' tacitly assumes the closure of a cell belongs to C_P. That is the frontier condition: closures of cells are unions of cells.
Small gap: the claim that each cell is closed in some open U in F needs justification, e.g. the open star of the cell. This is not stated.

ideas.what: Sheafify a family F of 'tame' subsets into a sheaf G_F of locally-F subsets inside the sheaf of germs of subsets, and take global sections as the closure F-bar.
ideas.modern_name: locally definable / locally constructible sets; sheafification of a presheaf of sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard sheaf theory; locally definable sets in o-minimal geometry (Delfs–Knebusch, 1980s)
ideas.where_published: Analogous local constructibility appears in EGA IV §9 and SGA 4 for schemes; not for this topological axiomatics.

ideas.what: Even for compact X, F-bar can be strictly larger than F when F does not generate the topology. Example: F = {∅, X} gives F-bar = the clopen subsets.
ideas.modern_name: clopen sets as global sections of the sheafified trivial family

ideas.what: For the family generated by a cellular decomposition, F-bar = F (and F-bar_U = F_U for all opens U in F) forces closed cells, and indeed all cells, to be connected. Sufficiency is asked here and proved on the next page.
ideas.modern_name: constructibility with respect to a stratification is local iff strata are connected
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather; Goresky–MacPherson)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is careful but routine foundational work: sheafifying a family of constructible sets and noting that stratification-constructibility is local iff the strata are connected. It is historically interesting as part of Grothendieck's 1974 tame-topology axiomatics, which predates o-minimality. There is no new result or unexplored connection.
